title: GH#1020: Kadence query loops skip the full REST API boot, theme mods decoded once; release 1.3.99
body:
## Summary

Two Kadence costs paid on every front-end page, fixed in **Fixes for other plugins** (on by default), and release 1.3.99.

- **Kadence Blocks Pro query loops** no longer boot the whole REST API. While a `kadence/query-*` block whose query has not run renders (no REST server running yet), `$wp_rest_server` is a `SEOProStack_Kadence_Query_Server` (new `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-query-server.php`) holding only `GET /wp/v2/kadence_query/query`, with Kadence's own callback, `permission_callback` and args. Kadence's own `rest_do_request()` dispatches there. The global is cleared as dispatch starts and after every block, so any other route or later REST use gets the full server. REST requests are untouched.
- **Kadence theme mods** are decoded once per request: `pre_option_theme_mods_{stylesheet}` (Kadence or a child theme) returns the value decoded once per site and stored string in `wp_load_alloptions()`, through `option_{name}` filters as `get_option()` does.

Not fixable here: Kadence Blocks 3.8.0 design tokens read `wp_kb_design_tokens` 268 times per page (`Token_Store` is `final`, and its DB layer has no short-circuit filter).

## Evidence

Web-SAPI profile, Burnaby network site `/service/construction-company/` (WooCommerce, MCP Adapter, Fluent apps, Ultimate Multisite), three alternating A/B pairs using the same mechanism as a request-local prototype:

| | Query block (inclusive) | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|

## What

New, on by default: **Links skip redirects** (Links tab). Links in posts, block widgets and menus to an old address that Rank Math permanently redirects to another page of the same site now point straight at that page when it is shown. Saved content is unchanged.

Resolves #1046

## Why

Renamed pages keep their old address through Rank Math → Redirections, but internal links still point at it, so each visit and crawl takes an extra 301. A client site did this with a must-use plugin no update reaches; this is the generic version.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-redirect-links.php` (`SEOProStack_Redirect_Links`, key `redirect_links`), listed in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES` after Modal links.

- Front end: `the_content` and `widget_block_content` (`WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`) and `wp_nav_menu_objects`, priority 20. Follows chains up to five hops and keeps fragments. Links with a query string are skipped, and HTML that mentions no old path is not parsed.

title: GH#1039: Load plugins only where needed checks each address and skips what it renders the same without; release 1.3.108
body:
Resolves #1039

## What

Load plugins only where needed skips more plugins on each address of the site. Plugins that add something to pages loaded on every page of their kind, even where they added nothing. Each address visitors open is now checked once in the background, and skips only the plugins it renders exactly the same without.

The first approach on this issue, verifying per page kind from sampled pages, failed on a test site: sampled pages had no form, so Fluent Forms was marked safe for every page, and the contact page lost its form (see the issue comment). This PR checks each address by itself instead of generalising from a sample.

## How

- `learn_front()` saves for each page kind the plugins it might also skip (`propose`): plugins that add to pages or extend one that does, but not the kind's needs, plugins that always load or check logins, or **Always load these plugins on the site**.
- `start_front()` keys a cookie-free address by its path plus `cpage`, `p`, `page`, `page_id` and `paged` (search results are not checked). It applies the saved skip set for that address, or queues it after a 200 render (at most 50 queued).
- The scheduled task `seoprostack_front_verify` (`includes/class-seoprostack-front-verify.php`) renders each queued address through a loopback: first as it is served, then without groups of the proposed plugins, halving a group when the page changes.
  - Each render carries a one-time token (`hash_equals`), is kept out of page caches (`DONOTCACHEPAGE` plus a unique argument), never learns or flags the site, and reports which plugin wrote to the database, sent a request or sent mail.
  - Plugins with such effects are never skipped, and a trial that adds effects fails.
  - A match needs the same status, key headers and cookie names, and the same normalised HTML. Up to 50 words that change on every render are tolerated, found by a second base render.
- Results go in `seoprostack_plugin_front_pages`. They hold until the content revision or the plugin set changes, for a week at most, and cover up to 5,000 addresses with shared skip sets. Five loopback failures in a row pause checks for an hour.
- The status panel shows how many addresses were checked, how many skip more plugins and how many wait. Uninstall removes the new options and the hook.

## Verification

On an isolated copy of a production site (45 active plugins, LiteSpeed, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.106 plus these files):

- 17 addresses were queued from visits and all were verified across 4 scheduled runs (about 50 s each). Single pages, the contact page, the home page, archives and pagination were among them.
- Cookie-free HTML compared with and without the saved checks was identical on all 17 addresses, apart from LiteSpeed's timestamp comments.
- Plugins loaded per page:

| Pages | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single pages | 36 | 20 |
| Contact page (keeps Fluent Forms; form present) | 36 | 22 |
| Archives | 39 | 34 |

- Server time to headers (median of 4 interleaved rounds):

| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Single page | about 620 ms | about 400 ms |
| Home | 531 ms | 441 ms |
| Directory archive | 540 ms | 535 ms |

- A search URL was not queued.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs and phpstan all pass.

title: GH#1061: WebP and AVIF images records a conversion only when the picture is unchanged; release 1.3.115
body:
## Summary

WebP and AVIF images could mark a picture converted while WordPress was still making its sizes, with a record (`_seoprostack_nextgen`) missing the later sizes. Media in cloud storage uploads only listed copies, so those copies stayed on the server, never sent or uploaded, and a storage drain with local removal on could not finish. Release 1.3.115.

Resolves #1061

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`
  - `GENERATION` post meta (`_seoprostack_nextgen_generation`), changed by `metadata_updated()` on every metadata save.
  - `convert_attachment()` reads the generation from the database before the sizes, and `unchanged()` compares generation, attached file and file names at the end. A change leaves the picture waiting (`nextgen_changed`); the next conversion keeps the copies made and lists every size.
  - `run_batch()` defers `nextgen_changed` pictures to the next batch; `wp seoprostack convert-images` passes over pictures that stay waiting after an error once per run (it could repeat them before).
  - `record_unlisted()`: converts a converted picture again when up-to-date copies of its files are missing from its record. The skip conditions match `convert_attachment()`'s loop, so a conversion always lists what it flags.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: `upload_attachment()` calls `record_unlisted()` after restoring removed files; when it changed the record, the picture is queued (which clears the retry job) and uploaded with its copies by the next batch.

title: GH#1064: Media in cloud storage names uploads from the claim index, not every stored record; release 1.3.117
body:
## Summary

With local copies removed, every `wp_unique_filename()` call read every stored inventory of the site (`stored_records()`) to list the folder's stored names. Production directory stacks paid 0.27s (1,385 stored pictures), 2.92s (15,221) and 7.24s (18,949) per call, several calls per picture, so bulk imports slowed as libraries grew.

WordPress only tests names that begin with the file name's stem (without a trailing `-N`): `_wp_check_existing_file_names()` matches `{name}-(size|scaled|rotated){ext}` case-insensitively, for the name, its numbers and other formats. So:

- `index_claims()` also stores a name claim (`n:{folder}\n{prefix}`) for each stored file under every hyphen-ended prefix of its lower-case name and the whole name (`name_hashes()`), in the existing `seoprostack_media_claims` table. The index is rebuilt for each version already, so no schema change.
- `unique_filename_files()` computes the stem (`numbering_stem()`), reads only the inventories under its claim (`stem_records()`: one primary-key lookup, then `handover_records()`), and returns only names beginning with the stem, local `scandir()` names included.
- Until the index is complete for this version, or when the lookup fails (`claims_failed()`), it streams every inventory as before, still filtered by stem.

Version 1.3.117 (plugin header, constant, readme, README, changelog).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`: all passed.
- Read-only equivalence check on production inventories (the branch's `numbering_stem()`/`name_hashes()` logic copied into a `wp eval-file` script, index simulated from every inventory): 3 stacks, 34,669 inventories, 846,160 names in this month's folder, 243 sample upload names (stored stems as uploaded, numbered, upper-case, size-like, other formats, new names); every name the full list holds for a stem was found through the index, and 15,480 `_wp_check_existing_file_names()` tests gave the same answer with the full and the index-scoped list.

title: GH#1084: Fluent Support email by IMAP saves sent ticket emails to the Sent folder; release 1.3.120
body:
## Summary

With **Fluent Support email by IMAP** on, every email Fluent Support sends a customer from that inbox is now also saved, exactly as sent and marked read, to the mailbox's Sent folder over IMAP. This keeps the support record in the owner's mailbox, as an email app would. Sending is unchanged: it still goes through the site's mail plugin (FluentSMTP through Amazon SES on the owner's site). Release 1.3.120: 1.3.119 was released for #1083 while this PR was open, and main is merged in.

- `includes/class-seoprostack-helpdesk-imap-sent.php` (new, `SEOProStack_Helpdesk_Imap_Sent`):
  - `mark()` at `fluent_support/mail_to_customer_header` (`PHP_INT_MAX`) marks the email when the ticket's `mailbox_id` is the feature's inbox. All five customer emails go through this filter: ticket created, agent reply, closed by agent, created by an agent, created on the customer's behalf.
  - `arm()` at `pre_wp_mail` hands the mark to the next `wp_mail()` only.
  - `sent()` at `wp_mail_succeeded` keeps the global PHPMailer's `getSentMIMEMessage()` when `From` is the inbox's address. The same works with core `wp_mail()` and with FluentSMTP's, which leaves the raw PHPMailer in the global.
  - At `shutdown`, `flush()` appends the copies.
  - A copy that fails waits in `seoprostack_helpdesk_imap_sent`, which is not autoloaded and holds at most 20 copies and 8 MB; extras are counted as not kept. `retry()`, called by the five-minute run, takes copies out of the queue before appending, so none is saved twice.
- `_Connection`: `folders()` and `append()`, with `\Seen`, the sent time as INTERNALDATE, CRLF line endings and modified UTF-7 folder names.
- Feature: settings `helpdesk_imap_sent` (on by default) and `helpdesk_imap_sent_folder` (empty means the first of Sent, Sent Items, Sent Messages, Sent Mail, INBOX.Sent, INBOX/Sent or [Gmail]/Sent Mail; a folder is never created). Also: boot, run (retry), the settings card and the `status` line.
- `uninstall.php` removes the queue option.
- Version 1.3.120.

Agent and admin notifications, FluentCRM and other site email are not copied, because their From address differs or they don't pass the customer filter. The inbox is still only read.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed, including phpcs and PHPStan level 8.

## Why

Sites send email from their own address: FluentSMTP's Force From Email is on, and Amazon SES needs it. The person who wrote in survives only as Reply-To. Tickets that **Fluent Support email by IMAP** made from these emails therefore belonged to the site, and agent replies went to the site instead of the person. This affected problem reports and MainWP Child's Contact Support form. The owner is routing Contact Support for every site to the WPALLSTARS support desk.

title: GH#1100: Kadence icon picker opens on press and shows at once; hidden Font Awesome animations no longer slow the editor; release 1.3.127
body:
## Summary

Kadence's icon picker still took a noticeable time to appear after 1.3.124. Profiling the preview site's editor (dark mode, every recommended plugin) found two causes.

1. **The page was slow on every frame, whatever was clicked.** Lasso Lite (Simple URLs 161) loads Font Awesome 5's SVG script on post editor screens. EventON Lite 2.5.10's tooltips (`<em class="evotooltip ajdeToolTip L fa">`) have Font Awesome's `fa` class but no icon, so Font Awesome turns each into its "missing icon", which has four `repeatCount="indefinite"` SVG animations. That makes 550 icons and 2,200 animations, all hidden in EventON's shortcode window. Chrome still ran them on every frame: a trace showed 2,200 `repeatEvent`s and 15,700 style recalculations in 2 s, with idle frames of 40-80 ms. Kadence's 100 ms debounce fired 265 ms late, and React's render waited one more frame.
2. **The picker itself.** It opened on the click (when the button is let go), then waited Kadence's 100 ms debounce, drew 150 icons per set and faded in.

## Changes

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php` (Fixes for other plugins, on by default): where `surl-lasso-icons` is enqueued, an inline script after it removes the `animate` elements of Font Awesome SVGs (`svg[data-fa-i2svg] animate`) whenever Font Awesome adds `fontawesome-i2svg-complete` to the html element. The icons stay, still. Font Awesome's own icons have no SVG animations. Its `showMissingIcons` option would not help: an element without an icon name gets the missing icon whatever it says, and for named icons it rejects the whole batch of replacements.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-kadence-icon-picker.js`: opens the picker on mouse `pointerdown` (the trusted click that follows is dropped so it does not close it again). Keys and touch still open it through the click, and a touch can still start a scroll. `FIRST` is now 50 (about a view's worth).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-kadence-library.php`: `.components-popover.kadence-icon-picker-pop-selection{opacity:1!important}`, so the picker shows at once. WordPress's slide, which carries its position, stays. No frame showed it away from its final place.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`: menu fitting's `flush()` walks changed subtrees with a TreeWalker that skips the insides of script-placed elements (inline left/right/inset/transform), instead of checking each of a popover's thousands of elements.
- Release 1.3.127: version, readme, changelogs and README.

body:
Resolves #1131

## What

Splits the Site templates feature (#1127) into focused classes, with no change in behaviour, so PHP Mess Detector (`phpmd.xml.dist`, which Codacy reads) reports nothing for it. Before: `SEOProStack_Site_Templates` had class complexity 382 with 32 methods, several methods over the cyclomatic and NPath limits, and the WP-CLI class was over them too.

## Change

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-site-templates.php`: keeps settings, scheduling, cron, the public `run()`/`undo()`/`manifests()`/`manifest()` API and constants, and one `locked()` helper for the MySQL advisory lock shared by apply and undo. It loads `includes/site-templates/` only when a template is listed, compared, applied or undone.
- `includes/site-templates/`, one job per class:
  - `manifest`: read, header/section/CSS checks, resources in write order (protected option names still fail at run time, as before).
  - `schema`: keyed items (pages, elements, images, parts) and menus.
  - `run`: site record, batches, cursor, journal (`journal()` then `amend()`, still saved before each write), `finish()`.
  - `parts`, `posts`, `media`, `menus`, `values`: one applier per resource kind, called in the same order as before.
  - `journal`: reads and restores the storage behind each journal entry type.
  - `undo`: identity recovery, preflight of every write before any change, ordered restore with per-write `undone` checkpoints.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-site-templates-cli.php`: the multisite loop (`all_sites`, `visit`, still `restore_current_blog()` in `finally`) is separate from each site's work (`list_templates`, `show_status`, `undo_site`, `run`).

## Summary

Resolves #1145.

- Retry transient HTTP/S3 failures up to three attempts with jittered backoff inside the batch budget.
- Preserve successful concurrent PUT/HEAD peers, checked payload bytes and existing size/digest removal checks.
- Keep an isolated removal failure local to its attachment; retain the site-wide pause for repeated service errors or configuration/credential failures.
- Document retries and recovery in README.md, readme.txt and changelog.txt.

## Files and reference pattern

Changes are confined to includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php, includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php and the three user docs. Uses the existing byte/concurrency caps and removal deadline handling.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: critical (local file removal). Testing level: runtime-verified.
Final head: ca7df534276ee17b1b79e68f0d3e09f85d3af698.

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed on final head (PHP/JS syntax, ShellCheck, actionlint, PHPCS, PHPStan; no JS build).
- Disposable WordPress 6.2/PHP 7.4 multisite, temporary subsite, with a localhost-only mock S3 endpoint: imported 120 PNG pictures (360 local files) through WordPress's media APIs, then drained the normal storage batch path in 13 turns. Result: uploaded 120, waiting 0, failed 0, local copies removed 120; every recorded local path absent, storage error empty, no site-wide wait. Rechecked the subsite's normal CLI status after installing final head.

A run on a request where Load plugins only where needed skipped plugins waits for the next. For each active plugin with a preset (here or network-wide), the differing paths go through `SEOProStack_Presets::write($slug, 'options', $paths)`, so the plugin's save code, the undo copy and `seoprostack_plugin_preset_changed` all run. The value written to each path is remembered in `seoprostack_presets_kept` (not autoloaded); a path whose stored value no longer matches was changed by hand and is left alone.
- Presets take a `manual` list (setting paths or option names; a path covers its children) that waits for Apply preset. Marked at the owner's choice: AI Engine's chatbot, Turnstile on Fluent Forms, Readabler's button and popup, Tutor LMS course rules (not `enable_gutenberg_course_edit`), Rank Math page schema, WooCommerce Order attribution. `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh` fails on a `manual` entry the preset does not set.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-defaults-keep.php` (new): remembers each own setting's default in `seoprostack_defaults_kept`. When a default changes, a setting still at the old one gets the new one. The first run switches on bool settings that default to on but are off (features made on by default after the site was set up). Network-enforced settings are skipped.
- `SEOProStack_Presets::paths()` (every path a preset sets, stored and wanted) and a public `same()`. WP-CLI: `wp seoprostack presets keep [--dry-run]`. Plugin deactivation clears both hooks; uninstall removes both options and hooks.
- Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `docs/presets.md`.

title: GH#1194: Load the CSS each page uses first; release 1.3.145
body:
## What

**Load the CSS each page uses first** (Speed tab, off by default) works only with the Kadence theme, Kadence Blocks (Pro), Kadence Pro, Fluent Forms (Pro) and WordPress's block library. For those, each page gets the CSS rules it uses inline, where each stylesheet link was. The full stylesheet then loads without holding up the first paint. The site's own server does all the work, with no cloud service or licence. FlyingPress 5 and LiteSpeed's UCSS both need one. This is a narrow exception, approved by the owner, to the no-CSS-optimisation rule in `AGENTS.md`.

This PR also releases **1.3.145**: the version bump, with #1192 (Keep pages cached, PR #1195), #1193 (Keep recommended settings, PR #1198), #1197 (network cache fills, PR #1200) and #1194.

Resolves #1194

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-used-css.php`:
  - Settings: `used_css`, plus two troubleshooting lists, `used_css_exclude` and `used_css_keep`.
  - When it runs: GET requests to front-end pages from people who are not logged in. It skips previews, the Customizer, feeds, embeds, robots.txt, AJAX, REST, JSON, AMP and any listed pages.
  - An output buffer on `template_redirect` at priority `PHP_INT_MAX`.
  - It steps aside where LiteSpeed Cache combines CSS or makes UCSS or critical CSS.
  - Changing any of its settings calls the new `SEOProStack_Page_Cache::purge_all()`, and turning it off removes its cache.
  - It provides the Recommended speed settings entry (`plan()`).
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-page.php`: rewrites one page. Each handled `<link>` becomes a `<style id="{id}-used">` with the used rules, in the link's place so the cascade is unchanged. After it come the link, with `media="print"` switched back on load, and a `<noscript>` copy.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-links.php`: chooses the links to handle. Each must be plain, render-blocking, local and inside a supported folder (filter `seoprostack_used_css_sources`, unsupported), and not on the keep list.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-match.php`: counts a rule as used when the page has every class, ID and element named in one of its selectors. This is an allowlist of selectors, not a list of whole stylesheets to leave out:
  - Classes that the Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Kadence Pro and Fluent Forms scripts add after load count as present. So do those from intl-tel-input, Choices and flatpickr.
  - The list is in `CLASSES`; filter `seoprostack_used_css_classes` adds to it.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-parser.php`, `-selector.php` and `-sheet.php`: parse each stylesheet once for each path, size, modified time and folder. The limit is 1 MB per stylesheet.
  - Each result is saved to `uploads/seoprostack-used-css/*.json` through a temporary file that is then renamed.
  - Rules inside `@media`, `@supports`, `@container`, `@layer` and `@scope` are filtered too.
  - Other at-rules are kept, except `@charset`, and relative `url()`s are made absolute.
- Uninstall and deactivation remove the folder. Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `AGENTS.md`.
- Release 1.3.145:
  - `seoprostack.php` (`Version:` and `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION`), `readme.txt` (`Stable tag:` and the changelog) and `README.md` (`Version:`, the badges and the changelog).
  - In `changelog.txt`, the Unreleased section is now 1.3.145.
  - `readme.txt` is 10,179 bytes, under the 10 KB limit. Its 1.3.145 notes are short; `changelog.txt` and `README.md` have them in full.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`: everything passed (php, js, shell, workflows, phpcs, phpstan).
- PHPMD (`phpmd.xml.dist`) is clean on all seven Used CSS files. `class-seoprostack-speed-plan.php` changes by one line, and its existing PHPMD findings are the same as on `main`.
- Disposable site (`scripts/test-site.sh`): PHP 8.3, Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms and WP-Optimize's page cache. The test page has Kadence's header, Kadence Blocks rows, tabs and an accordion, and a Fluent Forms form.
  - Render-blocking stylesheets: 11 before, none after. 41.0 KB of their 187.7 KB is inlined.
  - Median first paint under mobile throttling: 1,048 ms before, 824 ms after.
  - Parsing all 11 stylesheets the first time took 10.1 ms. With the cache files, each page after that took 5.4 ms.
  - Playwright screenshots of 9 states, on desktop and mobile: the top of the page, tabs, the accordion, form errors, the submenu and the mobile drawer. All 18 shots match the reference with the feature off. Some runs blocked the full stylesheets, so only the inlined CSS applied, and they matched too.
  - Splitting the classes for PHPMD left the rendered page the same, byte for byte, apart from a script version timestamp. The test used a fresh cache and a purged page cache. 11 cache files were written, no temporary files were left over, and the debug log is empty.
- The 10 CodeRabbit findings fixed in `1be93572` and `83d0ed30` were checked against 281 stylesheets and 52 link tags. The reply explains the 2 findings left as they are: https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprostack/pull/1199#issuecomment-6623255274
- After merging `main` (#1200) and bumping the version, `scripts/preflight-release.sh` gave 0 errors and 2 warnings, both already there before this PR. One is the WordPress.org slug note. The other is two core files that differ from the starter, which this PR does not change.
